chapters.title: Campaigns
chapters.subtitle: Name the work, and roll it up

steps.text: A campaign is a named push of work, such as a spring lead drive. This video shows why campaigns and campaign groups exist, how to create them, and where they are used by loads, agents and reports.
Calling, texting and follow-up work needs a name. Without one, a report cannot tell a spring lead drive from a round of renewal reminders.
For the outbound dialer, the name matters even more. Agents sign in to a campaign to receive the dialer calls of that campaign.
Related campaigns can be rolled up. A campaign group shows several campaigns as one line in reports, such as every campaign of a season.
A campaign only groups and reports work. It does not choose the channel, the number used, or what happens after each outcome.
Open Interaction Center, Management, Campaign Groups. A group is optional. If you want to roll campaigns up in reports, click Add campaign group.
Enter a Name and an optional Description, then click Save. The group appears in the list, ready to be picked by campaigns.
Open Campaigns, in the same Management menu, and click Add Campaign.
Enter a Name. Pick a Campaign group, or leave No campaign group. Add an optional Description, so people know what the campaign is for.
Click Save. The campaign appears in the list, with its name and the person who created it.
A second campaign, Renewal reminders, has no group. It is added the same way, and the list now shows both.
Campaigns and campaign groups cannot be deleted, because activities and reports keep pointing at them. Moving a campaign to another group also changes how its past activities are grouped in reports.
Agents sign in only to the campaigns on their entitlements. Open Agent entitlements, click Add, and pick the user, here jamie.chen.
Allowed campaigns lists the campaigns the agent may sign in to. Pick Spring lead drive. Allowed queues are for inbound work, and are set on the same page.
Click Save. The agent now sees Spring lead drive in the Work tab of the soft phone, and can sign in to it. Removing a campaign here also signs the agent out of it.
A manager creates the campaign, and adds it to the entitlements of the agents who work it.
A dialer load picks the campaign, and creates an activity for each contact in it.
Agents sign in to the campaign in the soft phone, and the dialer offers or places its calls.
Every call ends with an outcome on its activity, and the reports show the results by campaign and by group.
On an activity load, the campaign is stamped on every activity the load creates. Without one, the subject's Default campaign is used.
On a dialer load, the campaign is required, unless the subject has a default one. It is the line of work that agents sign in to.
On an agent's entitlements, Allowed campaigns lists the campaigns the agent may sign in to.
In reports, the campaign and the campaign group are filters, so you can see the results of one push, or of a whole season.
One campaign for each push of work, such as a lead drive, a renewal round or an appointment reminder, keeps the numbers of each easy to read.
A group for each season, region or brand lets a manager see the total for all of them in one report line.
Calls and texts for the same push can share one campaign, so their results are reported together.
Name each push of work, group the related ones, and agents, loads and reports all point to the same campaign. Thanks for watching.
